why: Trending: 'talking objects' POV comedy is one of the most-cited rising animated Shorts formats. Every viewer owns these objects, so it is instantly relatable.

series.name: If Things Could Talk
series.style: 3D animated comedy look, everyday objects with cute expressive cartoon faces (big eyes, small mouth), cosy modern home and city settings, bright colours, vertical 9:16 frame
series.negative: text, letters, words, brand names, logos, watermark, blood, scary, blurry
rules: Each episode, one everyday object tells its side of the story in first person, like a funny diary of its day.
The object has a cute cartoon face. Describe it in every shot's action so it stays recognisable.
Relatable observational comedy that every viewer has lived through. No brand names.
Only include a fact about the object if it is common knowledge; never invent numbers.
End on a punchline in the last shot.

topics: A phone at 1% battery, begging its owner for a charger.
The alarm clock that everyone hates every morning.
The fridge at midnight, watching the owner open the door for the tenth time.
The umbrella that is always forgotten at home on rainy days.
A toothbrush's morning and night routine.
A lonely sock that lost its pair in the wash.
The TV remote hiding in the sofa cushions.
A ceiling fan working overtime in the summer heat.
The pressure cooker that loves to whistle at the worst moment.
A school bag on Monday morning.
A bent phone charger cable holding on for dear life.
An ice cube's last minutes in a glass of lemonade.
The rubbish bin on collection day.
An old phone retired to the drawer.
The bathroom mirror on a bad-hair morning.
moreIdeas: A pencil who keeps losing to the eraser.

The kettle that is always switched on and then forgotten.

A backpack zipper stuck at the worst moment.
